description: Two-panel EBSD inverse pole figure (IPF) orientation map group of a Fe–Mn–Al–C austenitic low-density steel, comparing two conditions. (a) is the IPF map labelled "M2-SS" (bottom-left) with a black 50 µm scale bar (bottom-right) and panel tag "(a)" top-left; (b) is the IPF map labelled "M2-30" with its own 50 µm scale bar and an IPF colour triangle inset at the top-right labelled 001 (red apex), 101 (green corner) and 111 (blue corner), i.e. the standard cubic/fcc orientation key. Both maps are rendered in the same random red/green/blue/purple/yellow grain colouring, with thin dark lines marking grain boundaries; individual grains in (a) contain straight internal line features suggesting twins or sub-boundaries. No axes, no numeric data labels and no boundary-misorientation scale are printed; the only quantitative anchor is the 50 µm scale bar in each panel. The two panels make one argument: the colour distribution is essentially random in both states (no strong texture), but the grain-size population changes — (a) shows a bimodal mixture of large grains with many small grains embedded between them, whereas (b) after aging shows a more uniform (unimodal) grain size with the small grains grown and the large grains largely unchanged.
measured_quantities: grain orientation (IPF colour, no numeric scale printed)
grain-size distribution (bimodal vs unimodal, stated qualitatively)

observations.observation: Both panels are EBSD inverse pole figure (IPF) orientation maps, each with a black 50 µm scale bar.
Panel (b) contains an IPF colour-triangle legend with corners labelled 001 (red), 101 (green) and 111 (blue), identifying the colour key as the standard cubic orientation triangle.
The sample labels printed on the maps are 'M2-SS' in (a) and 'M2-30' in (b).
Grain colours are distributed randomly (mixed red/green/blue/purple/yellow grains adjacent to one another) in both maps, with no extended regions of a single colour.
Panel (a) shows grains of clearly differing sizes, with small grains embedded between larger ones, i.e. a bimodal grain-size population.
Panel (b) shows a visually more uniform grain-size population than (a), with fewer small embedded grains.
No axes, numeric scales, misorientation values or grain-size values are printed on either panel; the only quantitative anchor is the 50 µm scale bar.
The caption states Fig. 2 is the inverse pole figure (IPF) of (a) M2-SS and (b) M2-30.
The citing text states the random colour distribution in both samples indicates the absence of significant texture in either state.
The citing text states that (a) M2-SS shows a bimodal grain-size distribution, with small grains that did not fully grow during solution treatment remaining around larger grains.
The citing text states that after aging (M2-30) the smaller grains grow slightly while the larger ones remain almost unchanged, producing a unimodal grain-size distribution.

subfigures.description: EBSD IPF orientation map of sample M2-SS (solution-treated state), colour-coded per grain with thin dark grain boundaries; many small grains embedded among larger ones giving a bimodal grain-size distribution; several grains contain straight internal lines (twins/sub-boundaries). Black 50 µm scale bar at bottom-right. No axes or numeric labels.

EBSD IPF orientation map of sample M2-30 (aged state), same colour coding, with an IPF colour triangle inset (001 red, 101 green, 111 blue) at top-right and a black 50 µm scale bar at bottom-right. Grain size appears more uniform than in (a), with fewer small residual grains.
